matchstick.title: Vertical sticks in simple numerals
matchstick.principle: I, II, III, and L consist only of vertical matchsticks, so adding or removing a single vertical stick changes the numeral’s value by exactly one per stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase or decrease the value of a simple numeral (I, II, III, L) by one using a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical from II to another token turns II into I (value –1).

matchstick.title: Preserve token validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, both the source token (with a stick removed) and the destination token (with a stick added) must still be recognizable Roman numerals or allowed operators (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before accepting the move.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from '=' yields '-', which is still a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Use numeric difference to guide moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of each side of the equation; the difference tells how many units must be added to one side or removed from the other.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, to decide which side needs adjustment.
matchstick.example: If LHS = 5 and RHS = 7, you need to raise LHS by 2 or lower RHS by 2.

matchstick.title: I‑V reordering changes value by 2
matchstick.principle: Swapping the order of I and V (IV ↔ VI) changes the numeral’s value by exactly two.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the expression contains the pattern IV or VI and you can move an I across a V without breaking token validity.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick from one numeral to another reduces the source’s value by one and raises the destination’s value by one, provided both remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust two numerals by opposite one‑unit changes.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from XVII (17) to X (10) yields XVI (16) and XI (11).

matchstick.title: Never take sticks from V or X
matchstick.principle: V and X consist solely of diagonal sticks; removing any of those sticks leaves an invalid shape, so they must never be used as sources.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider a stick to move, exclude V and X as possible sources.
matchstick.example: Do not remove a diagonal from X to try to make it I.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity
matchstick.principle: Operators may only be +, -, or = after a move; any other shape is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is moved from or to an operator token.
matchstick.example: Turning '=' into '-' by removing a horizontal is allowed; turning '+' into '*' is not.

matchstick.title: Final verification of equation
matchstick.principle: After the stick move, recompute the numeric values of the entire equation to ensure it is a true equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Just before submitting the final answer.
matchstick.example: Check that V = XVI - XI evaluates to 5 = 5.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick from '+' to numeral
matchstick.principle: Moving the vertical component of a '+' operator to a numeral turns '+' into '-' and increments the numeral by one (if the numeral can accept a vertical stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a '+' is present and a simple numeral (I, II, III, L) needs to be increased by one.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' to I changes '+' to '-' and I to II.

matchstick.title: Horizontal stick transfer between operators
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' (or vice versa) swaps the two operators: '-' becomes '=', and '=' becomes '-'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change an equality into a subtraction or the opposite without affecting numerals.
matchstick.example: Changing 'A = B - C' into 'A - B = C' by moving a horizontal stick.

matchstick.description: Taking a stick from V or X, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring that V and X are made only of diagonal sticks which cannot be removed without breaking the symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select V or X as a source for a stick; only tokens with vertical or horizontal sticks may be sources.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid one
matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving sticks without checking the resulting shape may produce a symbol that is not +, -, or =.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any operator modification, verify that the resulting symbol matches one of the allowed operators.

matchstick.description: Assuming a single stick can change a numeral's value arbitrarily
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model may think moving a stick can increase a numeral by more than one unit, ignoring the actual effect of a single stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recall that adding or removing a vertical stick changes a numeral by exactly one; moving a stick between numerals changes each by one.

matchstick.description: Neglecting to recompute the arithmetic after the move
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model may trust the move without checking if the new equation is true.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the numeric values of both sides after the move and confirm equality.

matchstick.description: Treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical sticks
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model may move a diagonal stick into a vertical position or vice versa, violating stick orientation constraints.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: diagonal sticks stay diagonal; only vertical/horizontal sticks may be moved to vertical/horizontal positions.
